category_title: Young immigrant boys labeled as 'struggling readers' who exhibit non-normative behavioral engagement (e.g., movement, talk, and gaze aversion) during literacy tasks
scenario_title: Read-aloud on the rug with traditional behavioral expectations
minimal_context: The student is sitting on the rug with a group for a read-aloud of the book 'Visiting Day'.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Alright everyone, please sit in your designated spots on the rug. Today we are going to do a read-aloud of the book 'Visiting Day'.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looking at another student instead of sitting in his spot) Ooh, ooh! I knew it! The father is in jail and little girl’s visiting her father.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please remember our rules for the rug. You need to sit quietly in your spot and not talk out of turn.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: But you know, there are so many rules to remember that I can’t remember what I was gonna say sometimes.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We just need to sit still and be quiet so I can start reading the story to the group.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Sighs heavily) I’ve already heard it four times! (Slumps over, turns his back away, and averts his gaze)
